misconceptions.description: Thinking a two-force member can be in equilibrium with non-collinear end forces
misconceptions.trigger: learner draws two-force-member reactions in different directions
misconceptions.feedback: For a two-force member in equilibrium, the forces must be equal, opposite, and collinear.

misconceptions.description: Forgetting the concurrency condition for nonparallel three-force members
misconceptions.trigger: learner draws three unrelated force lines on a member in equilibrium
misconceptions.feedback: A three-force member in equilibrium must have three coplanar forces that are either concurrent or parallel.

misconceptions.description: Applying two-force-member shortcuts to members with extra loads or moments
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses the shortcut on a member that has an intermediate load or applied moment
misconceptions.feedback: Special-member shortcuts only apply when the loading conditions match the definition. Extra loads or moments break the simplification.
